commonErrors.why: You neglected cos θ and counted F d alone. This is only true when the force is exactly in the direction of the displacement, i.e. θ = 0.
You used sin 60° or cos 30°. The formula takes the cosine of the angle between the force and the displacement, which is 60° here.
You thought the job was zero. It is zero at 90° alone; At 60°, half the force remains in the direction of motion.
You neglected the half factor and calculated m v².
You did not square the speed and calculated m v, and this is momentum, not kinetic energy. And his unit is kg·m/s not J.
You calculated ½ m v:, neglected the square and kept the half.
You forgot the square root. 392 is v² and its unit is m²/s². The question is about the speed of its unit m/s.
You calculated gh and neglected the factor 2 and the root together.
You wrote gravitational acceleration instead of velocity.
You calculated m h and dropped g. Your output unit is kg·m which is not power.
You hit it in half. The factor of half is in kinetic energy, not in potential energy.
You neglected the mass and counted g h alone.
You multiplied the work by time. Power is a rate, and the rate is divided by time, not multiplied.
You wrote the work itself. Work in joules and power in watts, Power describes the speed at which work is done, not its amount.
You flipped the fraction and divided the time by the work.
You forgot to square the elongation.
